[[File:Great dodecicosahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great dodecicosahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''great dodecicosahedron''' (or '''great dodekicosahedron''') is a [[nonconvex uniform polyhedron]], indexed as U<sub>63</sub>. It has 32 faces (20 [[Hexagon|hexagons]] and 12 [[Decagram (geometry)|decagrams]]), 120 edges, and 60 vertices.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathconsult.ch/static/unipoly/63.html|title=63: great dodecicosahedron|last=Maeder|first=Roman|date=|website=MathConsult|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> Its [[vertex figure]] is a [[quadrilateral#Complex quadrilaterals|crossed quadrilateral]].

It has a composite [[Wythoff symbol]], 3 {{frac|5|3}} ({{frac|3|2}} {{frac|5|2}}) |, requiring two different [[Schwarz triangle]]s to generate it: (3 {{frac|5|3}} {{frac|3|2}}) and (3 {{frac|5|3}} {{frac|5|2}}). ('''3 {{frac|5|3}} {{frac|5|2}}''' '''|''' represents the ''great dodecicosahedron'' with an extra 12 {{mset|{{frac|10|2}}}} pentagons, and 3 {{frac|5|3}} {{frac|3|2}} | represents it with an extra 20 {{mset|{{frac|6|2}}}} triangles.)<ref>{{cite book | first=Magnus | last=Wenninger | author-link=Magnus Wenninger  | title=Polyhedron Models | publisher=Cambridge University Press | year=1974 | isbn=0-521-09859-9 }} pp.&nbsp;9–10.</ref>

Its [[vertex figure]] 6.{{frac|10|3}}.{{frac|6|5}}.{{frac|10|7}} is also ambiguous, having two clockwise and two counterclockwise faces around each vertex.

== Related polyhedra ==

It shares its [[vertex arrangement]] with the [[truncated dodecahedron]]. It additionally shares its [[edge arrangement]] with the [[great icosicosidodecahedron]] (having the hexagonal faces in common) and the [[great ditrigonal dodecicosidodecahedron]] (having the decagrammic faces in common).
